shared_elements: low-relief carving on a large rectangular stone block/pillar
weathered buff limestone surface with pitting
figures stacked one above another on a flat vertical face
surrounding dry-stone rubble/masonry of an excavated context
justification: Both show shallow, flat-relief profile animals with reserved silhouettes cut into a weathered buff limestone slab, stacked in vertical tiers on the block's front face, and both sit in an excavated rubble setting, which makes the immediate impression quite close. The clearest difference is density and content: A is packed with abstract registers (a row of arch/loop motifs, a hatched band, a disc) alongside its birds, whereas B carries only two or three sparsely spaced quadruped/reptilian figures with no geometric ornament.
